title: Comment on: Cloudflare acquires Deno
body:
I'm happy that the Deno team found a suitable home. Cloudflare is likely the best place for them to land.
I believe they will do great things together. However, I'm a bit concerned that there are very few independent Node.js runtimes: Anthropic acquired Bun, and now Deno will not be developed further.
Somehow I don't believe that Cloudflare doubling down on their own runtime -workerd, which will be likely migrated to Rust soon [1]- is the right choice (since it push on semantics that can only be run on Cloudflare infrastructure). I strongly believe Node.js semantics are likely the right ones for agents.
If anyone is looking for a full-open source alternative to Node.js that can run everywhere (browsers, phones or servers), please be aware that you can rely and use Edge.js [2] (disclaimer: Edge.js is part of the company that I founded: Wasmer)

title: Comment on: Programming Isn't Special
body:
I have been programming for 16 years now. I am glad AI arrived because I was getting sick of it anyway. You can’t call Art a form of plumbing different blocks together with business glue logic. It just highlights that we were plumbing all those frameworks and tools together in order to produce piece of code that businesses or individuals are willing to pay for.
When I was a junior developer I did see programming as an art but I really don’t see it anymore. What is important is the output. And does the output is in accordance to its design and functions as intended.
You can produce great software with any code or programming languages that you can think of. Some tools and practices produce them faster and/or with higher quality and correctness.
You can replicate the same product with almost any programming language now and good software practices now. AI makes the writing process a breeze but doesn’t solve what is art: the design and the vision (why and what). Therefore I think you can’t call the process of production an art. It’s really not that special.

title: Comment on: Scam American companies are using to manipulate ingredient lists
body:
It's all processing. 
Wool is a free by-product, sheep have to be sheared. 
More than 20 years ago, it was a pretty lump sum for someone who would shear 10K sheep a year. Still not much compared to the shearing price, but that helps sheep get more meat, reduce disease problems, and also reduce their size to the feeding stations. So a win for everybody.
Then, everything closed and the only thing left was to send it to China. Priced dropped entirely, to the point where it would mostly be considered a net negative. You have to store it before you can send a batch, and that takes a lot space. Not only that, but it has to stay dry. Then, consider you want to have a basic sort already done, because you don't want the whole batch to be paid little because it would be considered the lowest grade. So Bags should be consistent; they also have to be dense enough to avoid taking too much space (typical bags are around 1 cubic meter / 100kg). Most of these operation require quite a lot of very tiring human labor, which also require some skills, a problem pervasive with the sheep industry.
So yes, in the end it's too cheap to produce but too expensive to buy.

title: Comment on: You might want to try being less creative
body:
The most creative things I've done have come from stealing ideas. My longest running project has been sewing. I was tired of buying shirts and them not fitting, so I went out on a journey to reproduce a shirt I owned that fit perfectly. I designed the pattern, made the software to design the pattern, learned how to sew, and a year later I have a perfectly fitting T shirt (with my own adjustments to the original inspiration).
I made a replica of a watch that was too expensive. I made a pair of shoes because the real version was too expensive. I made illustrations based off other art.
I'm an engineer who likes art, not an artist who likes engineering. Stealing ideas, making your process efficient, and creating a great product are all what's important to me... not something like capturing my raw and original emotions in the work.

title: Comment on: Yes, and
body:
They very well might when it's outside the core remit of the company. Companies do this all the time - outsource/subcontract work so they can focus on what they're good at.
Yes, they might be able to build software that works for (relatively) close to free now. But that still has marginal cost in terms of extra resource to build it. Then it needs to be maintained, upgraded to meet changing internal requirements, it needs to be secure, they need to be able to trust it does what it's supposed to.
Sure, the cost of all of that has come down, but it's still a lot of work when they could just entrust another company to do that for a cost they're willing to pay. And companies are often happy to pay a lot in B2B contracts.
Just to reinforce this: look at the cost savings from cloud-exits - yet companies still readily build out in the cloud. FOSS has existed for decades, yet companies still pay for proprietary alternatives. Build vs buy exists on more dimensions than just cost alone.

title: Web push notifications server
body:
Most modern browsers support web push notifications as well as the two big mobile OSes. I've a few services that currently use a chat service and a cli client to generically send notifications from various apps. I'd like something similar without being tied to a chat client.

So here's what I need

Something self hosted
I need to be able to run this behind ngnix as a proxy ideally
language isn't important but I need instructions to run it. I can do docker if need be, but ideally something I can set up myself on whatever linux distribution I choose (I'll likely run this in a incus container with ubuntu)
I need to be able to create accounts for one or more user
I need to be able to create notifications that I can opt in per machine/notifications, and trigger them individually. A webUI to manage, and subscribe would be ideal
I'd want to be able to trigger those notifications from another machine, with some kind of authentication, either via something like curl or a CLI I can run on the triggering machine
I don't have the skills to write it myself, so something pre-existing and maintained ideally

title: Cotswold District Council: CotswoldsPlus Local Visitor Economy Data Platform to Include Support and Maintenance
body:
CotswoldsPlus Local Visitor Economy Partnership (LVEP) seeks a suitably qualified provider to deliver a data platform that provides an excellent overview of the performance of the regional visitor economy, that helps to establish regional measurement standards for visitor economy performance, and provides deep insights into visitor demographics, attitudes and behaviour, as well as economic trends within the visitor economy.
The platform will be designed to deliver on the following:
1. Switching emphasis from driving visitor numbers to driving higher quality of engagement and volume of spend.
2. Dispersal of visitors to reduce over-tourism in some LVEP destinations and growing visits in others.
The requirement is for the creation of a data platform that can:
• Link to and ingest data from varied sources
• Display live and ingested data in user-friendly ways
• Allow for custom reporting
• Produce useful insights from all data
• Provide an access permission structure that facilitates easy administration across multiple partners and user groups
